newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 4.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - July 4.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Friday and main factors likely to affect trading:
* Investors are likely to stay defensive with higher domestic interest rates, Sun Hung Kai Securities said in its daily outlook.
* Any losses may be capped by the expected release of almost steady inflation figures for June, said Noel Reyes, vice-president at Anscor-Hagedorn Securities.
* BPI Securities said concerns on forex volatility will soon ebb as the focus shifts to corporate earnings.
* On Thursday, the Philippine composite index closed 22.47 points lower at 2,724.42.
* The Dow Jones on Thursday ended 100.43 points up at 7,895.81. PLDT's ADR closed up $1 1/4 at $65 3/8.
* The Philippine peso closed at its intra-day low of 26.405 to the dollar against 26.376.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was up at 24.3125 pct vs 15.09375 pct.
* The volatile Philippine peso stabilised on Thursday, lifting market confidence in the central bank's ability to wrestle currency speculators.
* The Central Bank said it raised its term reverse repo rates following the adjustment of its key overnight rate.

* Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said on Thursday the monetary authority is now a buyer of U.S. dollars after selling it heavily on Wednesday to quell peso speculation. He said the peso will remain market-determined despite calls for devaluation.
* The National Statistics Office is set to release June inflation data and exports figure for the first five months of the year at 9:00 a.m. (0100 GMT).

* A Reuters poll of five brokerages showed that June inflation is at 4.26 percent, almost steady from the previous month's figure and a 10-year low of 4.2 percent. Inflation in the year-earlier period was 9.8 percent.
* Power retailer Manila Electric Co said it has no plans to remove its A and B share classifications, president Manuel Lopez said.
* JG Summit Holdings Inc said it is interested to buy into the financially-troubled Victorias Milling Co.
